statements.markdown: **Proposition 10.9 (A finite-state restriction for the stated pulse family).** *For a “balanced pulse” family at location $m\ge2$ (radius $\rho=\lfloor(m{+}1)/2\rfloor$, parameters $0\le r\le\rho$, moving mass between positions $m$ and $m{+}1$ with the weighted total $2c(m)+c(m{+}1)=2\rho$ of the two coefficients fixed), if a predecessor state is constant across the whole family, then no function $\mathrm{decode}:\mathrm{State}\to\mathbb N$ can recover the parameter $r$ from $\mathrm{state}(r)$ for every $r$. The family has exactly $\rho+1=\lfloor(m{+}1)/2\rfloor+1$ members, so the fan-out is unbounded in $m$. More strongly, any finite set of states carrying an exact decoder for the family has at least $\rho+1$ elements, unbounded in $m$.*
